newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest seen hot this weekend, then cooler.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest seen hot this weekend, then cooler.

text.p: Temperatures were expected to climb above 90 degrees Fahrenheit in the U.S. Midwest this weekend but meteorologists said the heat wave would subside by early next week.

"We would be looking for temperatures to be getting into the 90s across much of the Corn Belt this weekend," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese Notis. "Today's weather maps suggest it might not last very long. Yesterday's maps had indicated it might have a little staying power."
A cold front was expected to move through the region late Sunday or early next week, bringing a chance for showers.
"The American model is indicating a nice cool-down with temperatures returning to normal early next week," Solberg said. "Whenever you go from warm to cold you always have the chance for showers."
Weather Services Corp's Joel Burgio said showers would push into Illinois at the end of the weekend or early next week. "That should spell the end of that current hot period," Burgio said.
CBOT corn traders said the market had been jittery over forecasts for persistent hot, dry weather which can hurt the corn crop as it enters pollination.
